source.title: Adversarial Attacks Leverage Interference Between Features in Superposition
source.authors: Edward Stevinson; Lucas Prieto; Melih Barsbey; Tolga Birdal

page_placements.theme: Consequences of superposition: adversarial vulnerability, noise sensitivity, interference errors

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies superposition and feature interference as mechanisms for adversarial vulnerability. It does not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether neurons have coherent jobs, so it does not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on superposition geometry and adversarial attacks, not neuron polysemanticity. The results below are recorded as related findings only (versions: none); cited claims about superposition and neurons are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The paper studies how superposed class feature vectors in toy bottleneck networks and ViT/ResNet/MLP-Mixer classification heads shape adversarial perturbations and their transfer. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, and never measures what share of neurons are polysemantic. Superposition is set up by design (dimensional bottlenecks, weight decay) and used as the explanatory frame. So no version V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that superposition interference geometry can create predictable adversarial vulnerability and explain attack transfer. They state superposition is sufficient, not necessary, for this vulnerability.
record.recipe_differences: No neuron-interpretability or polysemanticity measurement is reproduced; the study analyzes adversarial attacks and feature geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: In the attack-profile analyses, the reported correspondence changes with bottleneck dimension; in the no-explicit-bottleneck experiment it changes with weight decay and estimated effective dimension. Synthetic attack transfer also varies with input-correlation condition.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic bottleneck models, PGD perturbations align with theoretically optimal interference-based directions (cosine 0.92–0.97). Attack transfer rises from 5% to 98% as input correlations fix feature geometry across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition interference geometry predicts adversarial perturbation structure and transferability in toy classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: In ViT classification heads, latent–input attack-profile correlation rises with tighter bottlenecks (CIFAR-10: 0.16 to 0.89) and with weight decay lowering effective dimension (0.14 to 0.79).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tighter representation bottlenecks or rank-reducing regularisation increase interference-driven attack structure in image classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026), as stated in the text
record.problems: The paper itself says its insights stem primarily from simplified models and that superposition is not established as necessary for adversarial vulnerability. Its SAE feature analyses are described as preliminary and exploratory, and are not evidence about neuron polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported attack settings and architecture replications were not extracted because they concern adversarial attack behavior rather than any listed neuron-polysemanticity version. Exploratory SAE feature visualizations in Appendix E were also omitted; the text characterizes them as preliminary and the reported plots do not measure whether neurons have unrelated jobs.

untested.parts: No neuron-level activation analysis of image classifiers. Only class-head geometry and SAE feature counts.
No language models or MLP neuron measurements.
Superposition is imposed via bottlenecks and its effect on attacks is measured. Whether it causes neurons to respond to unrelated inputs is not measured.
Not tested. The m=k case yields orthogonal class vectors, and no neuron polysemanticity is measured.
Bottleneck ratio, weight decay and architecture are varied for attack-profile correlation and interference magnitude, not for the share of polysemantic neurons.
Not tested. SAE activation thresholds in App. E concern feature counts on adversarial inputs, not polysemanticity classification.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. 'Features' here means class readout vectors in a bottleneck head, not neurons. The paper cites Chan (2024), 'Superposition is not just neuron polysemanticity', which underlines the distinction. Appendix results (ResNet-50, MLP-Mixer, non-linear toy, attack families, CIFAR-10-C) are omitted under rows_left_out; they also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No measurements of individual vision neurons responding to multiple unrelated image inputs.
No language models, MLP neuron response measurements, or estimates of polysemantic neuron prevalence.
The paper tests whether superposed class-feature representations contribute to adversarial vulnerability, not whether capacity pressure causes neurons to respond to unrelated features.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Architecture and regularization are varied for attack-structure outcomes, not for the share of polysemantic neurons or the performance cost of reducing that share.
No neuron-level investigation of whether apparently unrelated activations share a feature or job.
No comparison of measurement ranges or explanation-scoring methods for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

relation.reason: Paper discusses superposition as a cause of adversarial vulnerability without testing polysemantic neuron claims; polysemanticity appears only in cited titles.

tranche.reason: Studies adversarial attack geometry under superposition in classification heads; no neuron polysemanticity measurement.

source_check.notes: Rows R1-R6 match Table 1. The transfer rows (R7-R9) belong to the Fig. 2 setting (k=7, m=2), not k=6/30/90. The 98% transfer uncertainty is ±11 in the text and ±1 in Figure 2. The v2 text is titled 'Adversarial Vulnerability from Interference Between Features in Superposition'. The study is about class feature vectors, not neurons.

statements.correction: PGD vs theory cosine 0.92-0.97 (Table 1, linear bottleneck, l2-PGD eps=0.2, 5 seeds); transfer 5% (uncorrelated) to 98% (global correlations), Sec. 4.3 / Figure 2.
